overall: Washington, DC is set up for an exceptionally hot Independence Day, with an Extreme Heat Warning in effect and a Heat Advisory covering the broader region. All NWP models and the NWS are in agreement on a dangerously hot afternoon, with heat index values potentially reaching 109-110°F. A 50% chance of showers and thunderstorms after 2pm introduces meaningful uncertainty — the NWS explicitly notes temperatures falling to around 96 in the afternoon, suggesting the peak may occur before convective activity arrives.
forecast_obs_notes: No current observations or hourly ASOS data are available yet, so assessment is entirely model-driven. The four NWP models span a 4.6°F range (NBM 100.6°F to HRRR 105.2°F), with the NWS point forecast of 102°F sitting near the lower-middle of that envelope. GFS (101.8°F) and NBM (100.6°F) are the cooler outliers, while ECMWF (104.1°F) and HRRR (105.2°F) lean notably warmer — the warm-model bias may reflect stronger mixing or delayed storm timing.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely TMAX is in the 101-103°F range, with the D1_NOW distribution putting meaningful probability mass across 98-105°F given model spread. The active Kalshi odd-bucket market tops out at 99-100°F (13.6%), but the NWS forecast of 102°F and model consensus around 101-104°F suggest the true peak likely sits one or two buckets above the modal odd bucket. The key risk is whether afternoon thunderstorms arrive early enough to cap heating — if they do, TMAX could slip to 98-100°F; if they arrive late or miss, 103-105°F is plausible. Confidence is moderate-low given storm timing uncertainty and absent observations. Best point estimate: ~101.5°F.
